$$I = \dfrac{C\sin\phi}{r^2}$$

$$r^2 = h^2 + a^2, \qquad \sin\phi = \dfrac{h}{r} = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{h^2+a^2}}$$

$$\begin{aligned} I &= C\left(\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{h^2+a^2}}\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{h^2+a^2}\right) \\ &= Ch(h^2+a^2)^{-\frac{3}{2}} \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{dI}{dh} &= C(h^2+a^2)^{-\frac{3}{2}} + C\left(-\dfrac{3}{2}\right)(2h)(h^2+a^2)^{-\frac{5}{2}}h \\ &= C(h^2+a^2)^{-\frac{5}{2}}\left[(h^2+a^2) - 3h^2\right] \\ &= C(h^2+a^2)^{-\frac{5}{2}}(a^2 - 2h^2) \end{aligned}$$

When $\frac{dI}{dh} = 0$:

$$\begin{aligned} a^2 - 2h^2 &= 0 \\ h^2 &= \dfrac{a^2}{2} \\ h &= \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}a \quad \left(\text{reject } h = -\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}a\right) \end{aligned}$$

When $h = \frac{1}{2}a$:

$$\dfrac{dI}{dh} = C\left(\left(\dfrac{a}{2}\right)^2 + a^2\right)^{-\frac{5}{2}}\left(a^2 - 2\left(\dfrac{a}{2}\right)^2\right) = C\left(\dfrac{5}{4}a^2\right)^{-\frac{5}{2}}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}a^2\right) > 0$$

When $h = a$:

$$\dfrac{dI}{dh} = C(a^2+a^2)^{-\frac{5}{2}}(a^2 - 2a^2) < 0$$

$\therefore$ When $h = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}a$, the intensity $I$ is maximised.

Let $V$ be the volume of water in m$^3$. Water flows out, so

$$\dfrac{dV}{dt} = -(4t - t^2)$$

Volume lost in the first $4$ minutes:

$$\begin{aligned} \int_0^4(4t - t^2)\,dt &= \left[2t^2 - \dfrac{t^3}{3}\right]_0^4 \\ &= 32 - \dfrac{64}{3} \\ &= \dfrac{32}{3} \text{ m}^3 \end{aligned}$$

Then

$$V(4) = 10 - \dfrac{32}{3} = -\dfrac{2}{3}$$

which is impossible. The pool cannot hold a negative volume.

In fact $V(t) = 10 - 2t^2 + \frac{t^3}{3}$ reaches $0$ at $t \approx 3.39$ minutes, so under this model the pool is empty ($0 \text{ m}^3$) before $4$ minutes.

If the question meant water flowing into the pool at this rate, then $V(4) = 10 + \frac{32}{3} = \frac{62}{3} \approx 20.7 \text{ m}^3$.
